title: Harborview Clinics — one report for five sites

tabs.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Harborview Clinics runs five outpatient sites. Each site manager currently keeps their own spreadsheet, and the executive team receives five differently shaped reports every month.
A single analyst has been asked to replace all of it with one Power BI solution. A first version exists and is being reviewed before it goes wider.

tabs.heading: Existing environment
paragraphs: Appointment and billing data sits in an on-premises SQL Server database. A separate staff roster arrives monthly as an Excel workbook saved to SharePoint.
The current semantic model imports every table in full and refreshes once each night. Refresh now takes over an hour and occasionally fails.
The model has no date table. Several measures compute year-to-date figures by filtering on a text column that stores the month name.
One report page holds fourteen visuals, including three that show the same measure at different grains. Site managers say it is slow to open.
All five site managers are currently assigned Member on the workspace so they can view the report.

tabs.heading: Requirements
paragraphs: Each site manager must see only their own site's rows, in a single shared report rather than five copies.
Time intelligence measures such as year-to-date and prior-year must work correctly.
Refresh must complete reliably, and the on-premises SQL Server must remain reachable after publishing.
Site managers must be able to view the report but must not be able to edit or republish it.
Report open time must improve without removing any of the information executives rely on.
The executive team wants a single monthly figure they can see without opening the full report.
